description: Reinforcement learning from human feedback: SFT, a reward model trained on human comparisons, then RL toward higher reward with a penalty for drifting from the SFT model.
A model trained to predict which of two answers people prefer; its score is the reward in RLHF. Its blind spots become the policy's exploits.
Reinforcement learning from AI feedback: an AI judge, often guided by written principles (Constitutional AI), replaces some human labels.
Direct Preference Optimization (Rafailov et al., 2023): learn from (prompt, chosen, rejected) pairs with a classification-style loss, without a reward model or RL loop.
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards: the reward comes from a program that checks correctness (answer matches, tests pass, constraint satisfied). Named in the Tülu 3 report.
Group Relative Policy Optimization (DeepSeekMath, 2024): sample a group of answers per prompt and reward those that beat the group average; no separate value model.
Training a small student to imitate a large teacher, today mostly by fine-tuning on the teacher's generated answers.
The model maximizing the reward in a way its designers did not intend, by exploiting gaps in the reward model or verifier.
